title: Tabla bols
summary: The tabla is a pair of hand drums of South Asia: a small treble drum, the dayan, and a larger bass drum, the bayan. Every stroke has a spoken name called a bol, and a rhythmic cycle called a taal is learned by saying the bols before playing them.
howToPlay: Listen: the pads light up as the computer plays one phrase of the cycle.
Echo: strike the same pads on the same beats when it is your turn.
The chart shows every beat of the cycle with its bol; the first beat of each section is marked.
Choose a ten-beat, a seven-beat or an eight-beat cycle.
rules: Jhaptal has ten beats grouped 2+3+2+3; rupak has seven grouped 3+2+2, and its first beat is the open one; keherwa has eight beats.
Dha, Dhin and Ge are deep strokes with the bass drum; Tin, Na and Ti are strokes of the small drum.
Timing is judged against the cycle; wrong or extra strokes cost points.
heritageNote: Tabla is played across India, Nepal, Bangladesh and Pakistan, in accompaniment to song, instrument and dance as well as solo. Students traditionally learn the bols by voice first, and a fixed pattern called a theka marks the cycle.
